verses.text: The three men stopped answering Job because he was right in his own eyes.
Then Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite, from the family of Ram, got angry at Job for putting himself in the right over God.
He was angry at Job’s three friends too. They hadn’t found an answer, yet they’d condemned Job anyway.
Elihu had waited to speak to Job because the others were older than he was.
But when he saw that none of those three men had an answer, his anger flared up.
Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite answered, “I’m young, and you’re very old. So I held back and didn’t dare tell you what I thought.
I thought, ‘Let age have its say. People who’ve lived many years should teach wisdom.’
But there’s a spirit in people, and the Spirit of the Almighty gives them understanding.
Being important doesn’t make people wise, and being old doesn’t mean they know what’s just.
So I said, ‘Listen to me. I’ll tell you what I think too.’
“Look, I waited for you to speak and listened to your reasoning while you worked out what to say.
I gave you my full attention, but none of you convinced Job or answered what he said.
Don’t go saying, ‘We’ve found wisdom. God can prove him wrong. No human can.’
Job hasn’t aimed his words at me, and I won’t answer him with your arguments.
“They’re stunned. They’ve stopped answering. They don’t have a word left to say.
Should I keep waiting while they stand there in silence with nothing more to say?
I’ll give my own answer. I’ll tell you what I think too.
I’ve got so much to say. The spirit inside me won’t let me hold it back.
My chest is like wine with no way to vent, like new wineskins about to burst.
I’ll speak so I can get some relief. I’ll open my mouth and answer.
Please, let me show no favoritism or give anyone a flattering title.
I don’t know how to flatter people. If I did, my Maker would soon take me away.
